---
title: "Authoring and support"
---

## Start with a native export

Install STACK SymPy and AI Feedback in your Quarto project, and install SymPy in the Python environment Quarto uses:

```bash
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback
python -m pip install 'sympy==1.13.3'
```

Add the question filter to `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters:
  - stack-sympy
```

Use a Moodle STACK export whose root is `<quiz>` and whose questions use `<question type="stack">`. Keep the normal question, input, PRT, deployed-seed, and qtest elements. Point a `stack-question` block at its XML path and exact `<name><text>…</text></name>`. The filter embeds a selected question and precomputes the requested variants when Quarto renders. Unchanged native XML remains the source of truth and can be imported back into Moodle. Port-only Python tests and resizable matrix settings need adaptation for Moodle; see [Python answer tests](python-checker-api.qmd).

```{.stack-question}
#| file: ../questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| seed: 17
#| variants: 3
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
```

Run `quarto render`, then serve the generated site over HTTP. The [README](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#install-in-a-quarto-project) also covers local development setup.

The learner submits in two steps: **Validate answers** parses the current fields and displays the expression form (for example, `x+x` rather than a simplified `2*x`), then **Check answer** grades that validated response. Editing any field invalidates the preview, so the learner must validate again. This explicit check mirrors the question input verification setting and helps learners catch syntax errors before grading. The polynomial example sets `<insertstars>1</insertstars>`, so `x**2+8x+15` previews as one sum and receives full credit in its first variant.

Below a rendered question, **Show source** reveals its authored Quarto fenced block and **Show STACK source** reveals the original XML file contents. Both panels start closed; they are available for inspecting and copying a working example.

The options are `file` and `question` (required), `seed` (signed integer, default 1), `variants` (1–20, default 1), `review` (`true` or `false`, default false), and `diagnostics` (`true` or `false`, default false). `feedback: true` opts a card into the [shared AI Feedback extension](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback); cards without it need no AI dependency. Install both extensions in the same project; feedback requires AI Feedback 0.8.0+ and Quarto 1.8.27+. `context: auto` (default) uses nearby visible prose; `context: none` omits it; `context: id1,id2` includes tagged blocks such as `::: {#id1 .ai-context}` (`.ai-feedback-context` and `.math-exercise-context` are shared aliases). `feedback-language` sets the explanation language (default document `lang`). `feedback-policy` selects an existing named policy from `ai-feedback.policy-files` or page policy files. A stable `label` targets exercise-specific policy settings; otherwise the card ID is used. The shared mathematics policy (`math-exercise`) supplies the default hints and is also the YAML integration namespace for STACK cards. A fixed seed reproduces a variant within this implementation. It does not promise the same pseudo-random sequence as Moodle's Maxima backend.

Feedback uses a learner's current answer, visible question text and selected context. A preceding matching **Check answer** can contribute minimal result status, finite score; XML, source panels, teacher answers, qtests, grader configuration, grader feedback messages and answer notes are excluded. It never grades a response or replaces **Validate answers** and **Check answer**. The shared settings panel lets a learner choose copy-prompt mode or configure their own compatible provider; no API key is placed in the page. The same [explicit teaching policies](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback/blob/main/docs/feedback-policies.md) are inherited across integrations, using `math-exercise` for STACK's mathematics policy namespace.

## Choose a teaching policy

The shared `math-exercise` defaults offer four steps, ending with a worked
solution. Loading policy definitions does not select them. The example site
loads [feedback/course.yml](../feedback/course.yml) and explicitly selects its
course policy in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  policy-files: feedback/course.yml
  project-policy:
    math-exercise: course-mathematics
```

A policy can inherit those defaults and specialize them by name:

```yaml
# feedback/course.yml
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    course-mathematics:
      max-words: 120
      reset-on-run: true
    brief-mathematics:
      extends: course-mathematics
      max-words: 90
    two-step-practice:
      extends: brief-mathematics
      steps:
        - step-prompt: Ask one guiding question without giving a formula or answer.
        - step-prompt: Give a concise worked explanation of this task.
          allow-full-solution: true
```

Select the specialization with `#| feedback-policy: two-step-practice` on a
feedback-enabled STACK block. `#| label: rational-practice` gives it a stable
key for YAML `exercises.math-exercise` overrides. `examples.qmd` also selects
`page-policy: {math-exercise: brief-mathematics}` in its front matter. Its other
cards inherit four steps; only the selected card replaces the sequence with
two. Omitted fields inherit, while a supplied `steps` list replaces every step
and its permissions. `base-prompt` changes the continuing teaching instructions;
`step-prompt` describes one step. Use neither the retired `prompt` field nor
an authored `integrations`/`defaults` section.

Edits clear stale feedback and Check evidence while preserving hint progress.
Check resets progress by default; a selected policy can set `reset-on-run: false`
to preserve it. Selecting a different variant always restarts progress. Feedback
collects a snapshot without running validation, grading, or authored tests.

## What the adapter checks

Before moving a graded question from Moodle, decide what a correct answer means
and check that its input and answer test are supported here. The [worked
examples](../examples.qmd) show form, value, numerical precision and matrix
questions. This guide covers the current limits; it does not claim every STACK
or Maxima feature.

| Teaching task | Supported choice | Check before publishing |
|---|---|---|
| Equivalent algebra | `AlgEquiv` | State any domain restrictions in the prompt. The supported expression grammar is narrower than Maxima's. |
| A particular written form | `EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac` or `LowestTerms` | Select the form test that matches the instruction, then test an equivalent answer in the wrong form. `LowestTerms` checks form without comparing the teacher value; pair it with a value check when needed. |
| A measured number | `NumAbsolute`, `NumRelative` or `NumDecPlaces` | Choose absolute or relative tolerance, or require written precision including trailing zeros. |
| A finite list or set | `AlgEquiv`, `Sets`, `SameType` or `EqualComAss` | Decide whether order, repetitions and written form matter. Nested members must be scalar expressions. |
| A matrix | `AlgEquiv`, `SameType` or `EqualComAss` | Choose fixed or learner-selected dimensions. See [matrix input](matrix-input.qmd). For any basis or a matrix meeting conditions, use [Python answer tests](python-checker-api.qmd). |
| Scoring and feedback | Weighted PRTs with branch scores, notes and feedback | Run the question's `<qtest>` cases and inspect wrong answers and alternate correct answers. |

The imported source must be a Moodle STACK `<quiz>` containing named STACK
questions. Question variables support a defined Maxima-like assignment and
arithmetic subset, including seeded `rand(n)`, exact matrices and selected
functions. Unsupported settings produce a build error. Fixed seeds reproduce
this port's variants, but do not reproduce Moodle's random sequence.

### Answer entry and form

A learner can enter algebraic or numerical text, finite lists and sets, or a
matrix. Strict syntax is required. With `<insertstars>0</insertstars>`, write
`2*x`; with `<insertstars>1</insertstars>`, adjacent forms such as `2x`,
`2(x+1)` and `(x+1)(x-1)` are also accepted. `xy` remains one variable and
spaces alone do not imply multiplication. Other insertion modes are not
supported.

`EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac` and `LowestTerms` examine what the
learner wrote, so their `sans` must directly name an input. `FacForm` needs one
polynomial variable in `<testoptions>` and factors univariate rational
polynomials; `SingleFrac` expects one written fraction or an equivalent atomic
answer. `LowestTerms` spots reducible written integer fractions and supported
denominator problems, but does not compare values or cancel symbolic polynomial
factors. When `questionsimplify=0` is used, the build checks that a teacher
form can be preserved. Decimal-place grading reads the submitted notation:
`17.50` has a different reported precision from `17.5`.

### Lists, sets and equations

Write lists in brackets and sets in braces; both may nest, and both may be
empty. Limits are 32 entries per container, six nesting levels and 128 total
collection nodes. `AlgEquiv` compares a list by position and a set by its
members. `Sets` reports outer duplicates and missing or extra members.
`EqualComAss` preserves written arithmetic, list order and repeated set entries.
`SameType` checks STACK test applicability, not exact shape: two supported sets
have the same type, and lists of different lengths can still have the same
type. Use a content test when contents matter.

Use exact fractions inside sets and in frozen author collections. Literal
decimals in direct lists have narrower support: constant arithmetic with
integer powers works, while decimal-bearing function calls, symbolic terms
and transformed author collections do not. Collection tests need a direct
learner input in `sans`. Author-only finite helpers include `set`, `setify`,
`listify`, `union`, `intersection`, `setdifference`, `member`, `subsetp` and
`cardinality`; use them in simplified question variables and freeze their
results before form-sensitive tests. See the [collection examples](../examples.qmd#nested-collections-and-written-form).

`AlgEquiv` also handles supported Boolean expressions, polynomial equations
and disjunctions, and elementary hyperbolic functions. For instance,
`a=0 or b=0` matches `a*b=0`, but a repeated-root equation is a different
answer. Equation, function and complex branch support is limited; review the
[precise expression limits](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#supported-subset-and-grading-behavior)
for a consequential question.

### Tests and evidence

Native `<qtest>` cases check PRT score, penalty and answer notes. Notes follow
STACK's ordered matching rules, so a terminal note can match after earlier
nodes have added notes. The test and review controls show results for the
chosen variants; they cannot establish complete parity with Moodle. For an
important assessment, also compare representative responses in Moodle.

## Validate and publish

For an extension-only installation, install `sympy==1.13.3` in the Python environment used by Quarto. Run `python -m stack_sympy.cli test --file questions/polynomial-expansion.xml` after placing `_extensions/stack-sympy` on `PYTHONPATH`, then render with `quarto render`. Serve the `_site` directory through an HTTP server, including locally: `python -m http.server --directory _site 8000`. Browser grading loads Pyodide and SymPy; its first use downloads runtime packages, so it needs network access. Review the generated question and run its qtests before publishing any assessment. If a source uses features outside the supported subset, `#| diagnostics: true` displays the location of a build error in the page during authoring; remove it for production so unsupported questions fail the render.

See [bounded matrix inputs](matrix-input.qmd) for fixed and learner-selected dimensions,
raw-cell handling and author decisions.

## Extend the Python port

`IsBasis` accepts any exact rational basis of the null, column or row space of
an authored matrix. Set the PRT's teacher answer to the original matrix `A`
and select `nullspace`, `columnspace` or `rowspace`. Set the input model answer
with `nullspace_basis(A)`, `columnspace_basis(A)` or `rowspace_basis(A)`; the
author need not enter basis vectors by hand. The older `columns` and `rows`
options compare spans with a supplied reference basis. `MatrixProperty` checks
integer entries, a determinant or identity. Authors can define additional
named predicates with `PythonChecker` and an explicitly selected module.
All of these use normal PRT branches to award marks. See the single
[Python answer tests](python-checker-api.qmd) guide for examples, API details
and the distinction from native STACK.
